description: CCRL-Blitz-anchored opponent pool for Sgurr calibration. Names must match fastchess PGN tags exactly. Anchors are the ccrl_blitz values below; the solve uses only this pool's games.

book.why: Generic and engine-neutral, within CCRL's 12-moves-per-side limit. Unchanged from pool-D.

engines.name: Bitfox-2.5.0
engines.build: bitfox.exe from bitfox-2.5.0-windows-x86_64.zip (zip matches its published sha256)

engines.name: Lynx-1.11.0
engines.build: Lynx.Cli.exe from Lynx-1.11.0-win-x64.zip, with its appsettings.json (online tablebase off, 1 thread)

notes: Built 2026-09-24 to measure version-to-version gains that carry over to CCRL, with enough resolution to see medium gains. Absolute accuracy is secondary.

Ratings are single-CPU CCRL Blitz from the live list updated 2026-09-21, checked twice. Every binary reports the exact rated version via `id name`, supports Hash, defaults to one thread, and has no own book or tablebases.

Nine families from 3087 to 3362. 4ku 5.1 (3059) is dropped: v9.1 scores about 70% against it and games that lopsided carry little information. Bit-Genie 9 stays as the one low anchor so v9.0 is bracketed from below. Four new anchors at 3340-3362 keep the next few versions bracketed from above.
Rejected: Pedantic (its repository stops at 0.6.2, CCRL rates 2.1.0), Stash 37.0 (source only; a local build is not the binary CCRL rated).

Adjudication was tested and rejected. Replayed on 8,168 pool-D games, resign adjudication (3 moves at 1000cp, both engines agreeing) saved 8% of time but turned 22 Sgurr draws into losses; draw adjudication saved 1% and turned 28 Sgurr wins into draws. A version-dependent bias is not worth 8%.
Time control stays 10+0.1. A CCRL-equivalent control (about 1'+0.6" here) would cost about six times as much per game and could not resolve a medium gain in a night.
Solved on this pool's games only (games_dir). Earlier pools' PGNs stay in games/ and are not mixed in. pool-D is archived verbatim at pool-2026-08-D.json.
Every version is calibrated with the same opening seed, so two versions meet the same opponents on the same openings in the same order.
